deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 58r of 'R.Varia' is not a Riemann manuscript. It is a printed page, numbered 3 with signature mark '1*', from a Berlin University lecture catalogue (Verzeichniss der Vorlesungen).

It continues the law-faculty listings ('Rechtsgelahrtheit') from the previous page:
- Berner's disputations on criminal law.
- Heffter on civil procedure and international law, citing his 'Völkerrecht der Gegenwart', Berlin 1844.
- Schmidt on common and Prussian civil procedure.
- Richter's civil procedure practicum.
- Gneist on accusatorial procedure.
- Röstell and Collmann on international law.
- Heydemann on Prussian Landrecht.
- Kohlstock and Schmidt offering repetitoria.

It then opens the medical section ('Heilkunde'):
- Hecker on medical encyclopaedia and history.
- Simon on general anatomy.
- Johannes Müller on comparative anatomy, pathological anatomy and special physiology.
- Schlemm on osteology and anatomy of the sense organs.
- Schultz on medical natural history, human physiology and medical botany.
- Link on general physiology.
- Ehrenberg on the physiology of infusoria and on microscope exercises.
- Brücke on the theory of the microscope.
- Mitscherlich on pharmacology.
- Casper on prescription-writing.
- Ascherson on toxicology.

The page can be roughly dated from internal evidence:
- The previous page cites Kraut's Grundriss, 3rd edition, 1845.
- Brücke was still in Berlin, which he left in 1848.
- Dieffenbach, who appears on the next page, was still alive; he died in November 1847.

This places the catalogue around 1846–1847. That is consistent with Riemann's Berlin study period (1847–1849), so he presumably kept the catalogue or later reused it as paper. No derivation, formula, or marginal annotation by Riemann is visible. The only mark is a small stray sign in the right margin near the 'Specielle Physiologie' entry, which cannot be interpreted.

results.what: Printed Berlin University lecture catalogue page (law and medicine), c. 1846-47; no mathematical content

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed university lecture listing with no mathematics and no visible Riemann annotation. At most it is biographical context for his Berlin student years.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription renders the long-s forms as 'Procefs', 'Preufsisch' and similar. The print reads 'Proceſs', 'Preuſsisch' (ſ = long s), not the letter f.
The Brücke line is partly obscured in the image ('lehrt Hr. Dr. Brücke in drei- bis vierwöchentlichen Cursen'). The transcription's reading is plausible but that line is damaged on the scan.
'fortgesezt' is indeed printed so (period spelling), not an OCR error.
The small marginal mark at the right edge near 'Specielle Physiologie' is not transcribed and is illegible or insignificant.
